# Tokyo Business Trip Itinerary: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12

A practical 3-day plan for **1 traveler** based near **Tokyo Station**, keeping **work hours 09:00–17:00 JST** daily, one client dinner on **2026-03-11**, and at least **2 hours of evening sightseeing** each night.
Budget target is **USD 1,200 total excluding flights**, with a lean but comfortable split.

## Trip Plan by Day

### Day 1 — Tue, 2026-03-10: Arrival, setup, and Marunouchi evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

- **07:30–09:00**: Arrive in Tokyo, transfer to hotel near Tokyo Station, drop bags, quick refresh.
- **09:00–09:30**: Buffer for check-in if available; otherwise use lobby/business lounge.
- **09:30–12:30**: Work block 1 at hotel or nearby coworking space.
- **12:30–13:30**: Lunch near Tokyo Station; keep it simple and fast.
- **13:30–17:00**: Work block 2; reserve 15 minutes at the end for next-day prep.
- **17:00–17:30**: Commute buffer back to hotel and reset.
- **17:30–19:30**: Sightseeing in **Marunouchi / Tokyo Station area**: station architecture, KITTE rooftop, evening streets.
- **19:30–20:30**: Dinner: **soba, tonkatsu, or a set meal** close to the station.
- **20:30–21:30**: Optional light walk around Tokyo Station Marunouchi side or Imperial Palace outer area.

### Day 2 — Wed, 2026-03-11: Full workday and client dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/briefcase.svg

- **07:30–08:45**: Breakfast and commute buffer; leave extra time for meetings.
- **09:00–12:30**: Work block 1.
- **12:30–13:30**: Lunch with a quick, reliable option near the office/hotel.
- **13:30–17:00**: Work block 2.
- **17:00–18:00**: Buffer for freshening up and travel to dinner venue.
- **18:00–20:00**: **Client dinner** in a central business-friendly area like Marunouchi, Ginza, or Nihonbashi.
- **20:00–22:00**: Sightseeing for at least 2 hours: **Ginza night walk**, illuminated storefronts, department stores, and flagship streets.
- **22:00–22:30**: Return to hotel with a calm transfer buffer.

### Day 3 — Thu, 2026-03-12: Final workday and Asakusa evening

- **07:30–08:45**: Breakfast, check emails, and commute buffer.
- **09:00–12:30**: Work block 1.
- **12:30–13:30**: Lunch near Tokyo Station; keep it low-friction.
- **13:30–17:00**: Work block 2; finish all deliverables and confirm next steps.
- **17:00–17:45**: Buffer for packing and hotel checkout.
- **17:45–19:45**: Sightseeing in **Asakusa**: Senso-ji, Nakamise Street, riverside views if timing works.
- **19:45–20:45**: Dinner: **tempura, ramen, or yakitori** in Asakusa or back near Tokyo Station.
- **20:45–21:30**: Return to hotel or head to departure transfer.

## Budget Plan for 3 Days

| Category | Planned Spend | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel near Tokyo Station | USD 540 | About USD 180/night for a business-class stay |
| Meals | USD 210 | Breakfasts, lunches, one client dinner, 2 casual dinners |
| Local transport | USD 60 | JR/subway, airport transfer buffer, short taxi if needed |
| Work needs | USD 90 | Coworking, coffee, printing, incidental meeting costs |
| Sightseeing / misc. | USD 120 | Entry fees, snacks, small purchases |
| Buffer | USD 180 | Cushion for price swings and convenience |
| **Total** | **USD 1,200** | Excluding flights |

## Hotel and Daily Logistics

- **Best hotel zone**: Marunouchi, Yaesu, Nihonbashi, or Otemachi for easiest access to Tokyo Station.
- **Commute rule**: Keep all evening activities within **15–30 minutes** of the hotel on work nights.
- **Work setup**: Choose a property with desk space, strong Wi‑Fi, and early breakfast.
- **Dinner strategy**: Use casual lunches to preserve budget for the client dinner on 2026-03-11.
- **Transit buffer**: Add **15–30 minutes** before every meeting and **30–45 minutes** before dinner transfers.
